the pharmacokinetic profile of THU, in mice, is consistent with a low clearance, high volume of distribution and high bioavailability, which is consistent with its ability to inhibit cytidine deamination in the blood and tissues.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
THU pharmacokinetic properties in mice are similar to those in humans.
THU is a potent and selective CD inhibitor with a plasma terminal half-life of approximately 2 h in mice and approximately 4–8 h in humans.
THU has a plasma terminal half-life of 70–85 min in mice and humans, a 30–50% oral bioavailability in mice and rats and a plasma terminal half life of 1.3–2 h in humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
THU pharmacokinetic properties are consistent with its use in humans.
THU pharmacokinetic data in mice are consistent with those in humans.
THU is well tolerated, has a long plasma half-life, and has good oral bioavailability, all of which should facilitate the clinical evaluation and use of THU.
